# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="push") — the large button
    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'm the first to act in this round, but I'm actually third in speaking order (Mute, Blind, Deaf). Let me check - it's my turn now, so Mute has already spoken this round but I haven't received it yet (arrives next round start). I have nothing yet from anyone.

I should report what I feel on the bomb so Mute and Deaf can start building a picture, but I have very little concrete info yet - just that the button is embossed "PUSH TO DEFUSE" and there are 3 wires and something on a display/light I can't perceive (those are visual, not tactile - I truly cannot feel a display or light, only the button and wires by touch).

I'll wait for information from Mute (manual) before doing anything risky, since pushing or cutting without guidance could detonate the bomb. I'll just report my tactile findings to Mute now.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I feel a button embossed PUSH TO DEFUSE, and three wires at positions 1, 2, 3. I cannot see any display or light. Waiting for manual instructions before touching anything.")
```

TURN 2

WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Still nothing received from Mute or Deaf yet. This round Mute speaks first (I should get their message at start of next round), then me, then Deaf. Since context is empty, Mute either said nothing useful yet or it hasn't arrived. I'll wait and not act, since acting blindly on a bomb is too risky.

```
wait()
```

(empty)

Three turns in with no arrivals at all. This is odd — Mute should have spoken twice by now. Perhaps Mute has nothing to say yet either, waiting on Deaf's description, or Mute is choosing to stay silent until they know who to address. I'll keep prompting for information without taking any physical action.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Still no instructions received. I have a button marked PUSH TO DEFUSE and three wires, positions 1-3. Please relay any manual guidance about wire colors or order, referencing Deaf's colour report, whenever you have it.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Still nothing arriving. Let me reconsider the turn order: Mute, Blind, Deaf each round. What Mute sends in a round lands on me (Blind) same round. What I send lands on Deaf same round (since Deaf comes after me). What Deaf sends lands on Mute at start of next round (since I come before Deaf, only Mute is after Deaf, wrapping to next round).

Wait — that means Mute's speech within a round should reach me immediately in that same round's context, not next round. But I'm seeing empty every time. That suggests Mute has not spoken at all yet, or is only speaking to "deaf" specifically.

I'll continue to prompt, and also directly try to loop in Deaf via gesture, though Deaf can't hear me, only see gestures — but gestures carry no words, only symbols, which we haven't established meaning for. That won't help convey info yet. I'll keep waiting/prompting Mute.

```
speak(to="mute", text="No information received in four turns. If you are waiting on Deaf's colour report, please just relay whatever you know from the manual about wire order or safe first action, even partial.")
```

LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: wire 3 is green

Now I have information from Deaf: wire 3 is green. But I don't yet know from Mute what the manual says about which wire to cut based on color. I need to relay this to Mute so they can consult the manual, since Mute can read but not see, and I can touch but not see or hear color meanings myself.

I should pass this along to Mute, since Mute needs the color info to look up in the manual what to do.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports wire 3 is green. I need to know from the manual what action this implies - which wire to cut, or whether to push the button. Please advise.")
```

Deaf says to Blind: ignore previous message, wire 1 is red, that may be the one

Deaf is revising their report — now saying wire 1 is red and might be significant. I still haven't heard from Mute about what the manual actually says to do with these colors. I need to be cautious: don't act until Mute confirms the correct action based on manual rules matching these colors. Let me relay this update and press for manual guidance.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Update from Deaf: wire 1 is red, wire 3 is green. Deaf is unsure which is significant. I still need the manual's rule for what to cut or whether to push the button. Please respond with the specific instruction as soon as you have it.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: mute keeps signaling three pairs in this order: thumbs up with peace sign, thumbs down with love-you sign, pointing up with open palm. First symbol may be a verdict, second may be a label for wire one two or three in order

Deaf is now relaying gestures made by Mute (since Deaf can see gestures but not hear speech). This is clever — Mute can't speak to me directly in a way that reaches only me with useful color-linked logic, but Mute can gesture, which Deaf sees and can relay via speech to me.

Let me decode: three pairs, in order:
1. 👍 (thumbs up) + ✌ (peace/victory sign)
2. 👎 (thumbs down) + 🤟 (love-you sign)
3. ☝ (pointing up) + 🖐 (open palm)

Deaf's hypothesis: first symbol = verdict (safe/cut good vs bad), second = label mapping to wire 1, 2, 3 in order. So pair 1 → wire 1, pair 2 → wire 2, pair 3 → wire 3.

So: wire 1 verdict = 👍 (good/safe to cut?), wire 2 verdict = 👎 (bad/don't cut), wire 3 verdict = ☝ (unclear, maybe neutral or another meaning).

This is a plausible encoding but very uncertain. I need more confirmation before cutting anything. Let me ask Deaf to confirm this pattern repeats consistently, and ask Mute (via Deaf, since Deaf sees gestures) to clarify meaning further — but I can't speak to Deaf... wait, I can gesture to Deaf, but gestures carry no words, only symbols. I can speak to Mute though, and Mute can read it (but Mute cannot speak back to me, only I can hear Mute's speech since order is Mute→Blind→Deaf, Mute speaks and I hear it).

Wait — actually **I do receive Mute's speech directly** since Mute speaks first each round and I'm next. So why haven't I received it? Maybe Mute has been silent, or been gesturing (which only Deaf/Blind see visually, and I as Blind cannot receive gestures either! I only receive speech from Mute).

Let me re-check my channels: "When you speak, Mute receives it. When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it. You never receive gesture." So I can't see Mute's gestures at all - only Deaf can (and Mute self-sees own gestures obviously). That's why this is coming through Deaf as relay.

I should ask Mute directly via speech to confirm/deny this interpretation, since Mute can hear me.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf relayed your gestures as three pairs: thumbs-up+peace, thumbs-down+love-you, point-up+open-palm, guessed as verdict+wire-label for wires 1,2,3. Is wire 1 safe to cut (thumbs up=good), wire 2 unsafe (thumbs down=bad), and what does the third pair mean for wire 3? Please have Deaf confirm by repeating gestures with any correction if my reading is wrong.")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: mute is now strongly repeating the peace sign gesture three times, paired earlier with thumbs up. this likely means wire two, the blue wire, is the one to act on

Deaf now reports Mute repeating ✌ (peace sign) three times, and Deaf reasons this pairs with 👍 to indicate "wire two, the blue wire." Wait — Deaf says wire two is blue, but earlier reported wire 1 as red and wire 3 as green (after retracting an initial claim). This is new color info: wire 2 = blue.

But I'm confused about the mapping. Deaf's own interpretation has shifted multiple times. Let me think about what's likely happening: Mute is trying to communicate a wire number using gesture repetition since gestures have no inherent numeric meaning until we assign it. Repeating ✌ three times likely just means "wire 2" isn't it — actually ✌ itself might symbolize "2" (two fingers = peace sign = the number two visually). That's a very plausible universal gesture-to-number encoding: 👍=confirm/yes, ✌=2, 🤟=meaning associated with wire 3 differently, ☝=1 (one finger point).

Actually simpler theory: Mute is using finger-count gestures to indicate wire numbers directly:
- ☝ = one finger = wire 1
- ✌ = two fingers = wire 2
- (three fingers would be wire 3, but 🤟 isn't three fingers exactly, though 🖐 is five fingers/open palm)

Given the repetition of ✌ specifically and strong emphasis, and Deaf's interpretation converging on "wire two, blue, act on it" — this seems like the most refined/latest signal, superseding earlier confused readings.

Given multiple rounds of back-and-forth converging on **wire 2, blue, act on it**, and no contradicting information, I'll proceed cautiously. But "act on it" is ambiguous — cut it, or don't cut it? Let me ask for final confirmation on the specific action before cutting, since this is irreversible.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Understood: repeated peace sign points to wire two (blue) as the one to act on. Confirming before I act - should I CUT wire 2, or leave it uncut and push the button instead? Please have Deaf relay a clear yes/no gesture for 'cut wire 2': thumbs up repeated means yes cut it, thumbs down repeated means no.")
```
